decision_rationale: CERTIFY_DORMANT. The 600-Series dormancy is established by a ratified charter (S600 v1.0, DEFERRED), defended by a unanimous Executive Board vote (S724, 26/26), reaffirmed by two independent activation board decisions (S601 and S602, both KEEP DEFERRED, 21 convergent agents), and independently re-verified across all 9 success criteria by 8 S603 agents (B through I). All 4 mandatory activation gates are FAIL (Economic: -2.5 net sessions, Board: no new vote, Ownership: 3 conflicts unresolved, Baseline: no T0 captured). A comprehensive dormancy governance infrastructure is operational: 4 monitoring cadences (T0, Rapid Pulse, Deep Audit, Annual), a single authoritative Trigger Registry (4 gates, 3 triggers, 5 AV criteria, 7 prohibited paths, 5 economic assumptions), 6 drift detection signals (3 CRITICAL, 1 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM, 1 LOW), and portfolio dashboard integration. The economic case has worsened since the original deferral (Net -2.5 vs. Net -1.0), and no assumption change within the program horizon can flip the gate. Zero content changes, zero certification changes, and zero boundary violations occurred across all 600-series sessions. All 29 agents across S600-S603 converge on DEFER without a single dissenting vote. The only unresolved issues (GAP-3 ownership acceptance, C-001/C-002 CARRY_FORWARD conflicts, stale SESSION_STATUS) are governance-process items that do not block dormancy certification — the lane is dormant and governed whether or not the Governance Board has formally accepted the keys. The risk assessment rates overall risk as ELEVATED (not UNACCEPTABLE) due to governance execution failures in ownership acceptance and monitoring, but the automated DRIFT signals and charter prohibitions provide a floor of protection that makes dormant-state governance resilient to execution gaps. The 600-Series is DORMANT AND GOVERNED by design, not by failure. Certification is the correct governance posture.
